diagnostic_evidence.quote: suppose the set of limit points of $(x_t)$ is contained in a finite set $F_\ast\subset\RR^d$
This set is compact but, for $n-1\ge 2$, it contains a continuum of points.

issues.failure_explanation: For rank-1 approximation the limit set of a certified trajectory with $\delta_\ast<2$ is only known to lie in $(\mathcal M^\ast\cap\{\iapx(\delta_\ast)=0\})\cup F_{\mathrm{ng}}(\delta_\ast)$, where the first component is a continuum. Lemma lem:finite_limit_set requires the whole limit set to be contained in a finite set, so it does not yield that a trajectory with one non-minimizing accumulation point converges to it. Without pointwise (or at least eventual local) convergence, the center-stable-manifold/compact-covering exclusion that follows cannot be applied, leaving the a.e. exclusion of non-minimizing limits in the approximation case unproved as written.

issues.failure_explanation: Axiom (A6) requires, for every $\delta\in[\delta_{\mathrm{th}},\overline\delta)$ and every $x$ on the level set, that equality $I(\delta;\gd_\eta(x))=0$ hold only at stationary points. For the scalar certificate at $\delta=\eta$ the remainder $R^\sca(\eta)=\eta(\eta-\eta)(\eta^2-4)L^2$ vanishes identically, so every point of $\{\isc(\eta;\cdot)=0\}$ is mapped back onto the same level set and equality holds at non-stationary points. Hence the remark's claim that A1–A7 hold with $\delta_{\mathrm{th}}(\eta)=\eta$ is false at the endpoint $\delta=\eta$ (the level set $\{\isc(\eta)=0\}$ is invariant, so a trajectory starting there never has strictly increasing state).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Take $\delta_{\mathrm{th}}(\eta)$ to be any value in $(\eta,2)$ (or restrict A6 to the open interval $(\delta_{\mathrm{th}},\overline\delta)$), matching the strict inequality used in the scalar analysis.
issues.overall_effect: The verification that the scalar certificate is an instance of the abstract framework is wrong at the single parameter value $\delta=\eta$; results using strict initial inequality $\isc(\eta;x_0)<0$ are unaffected.
issues.title: Scalar certificate does not satisfy the stationarity axiom at the claimed threshold $\delta_{\mathrm{th}}=\eta$
issues.why_classification: A one-point endpoint correction that preserves every substantive claim.

issues.failure_explanation: Axioms A1–A7 are invariant under increasing reparameterizations of the state: if $P(\cdot)$ satisfies them with threshold $\eta$, then for any increasing homeomorphism $\phi$ of $(0,2]$ the family $\tilde P(\delta):=P(\phi(\delta))$ also satisfies A1–A7 on the same state space $(0,2]$ with threshold $\phi^{-1}(\eta)$ (nesting, positive definiteness, terminal set, state definition, and one-step monotonicity/stationarity are all preserved). Hence $P(\delta)$ is not uniquely determined for each $\delta$; what the Lagrange analysis can determine is the nested family of level sets (equivalently $P$ up to reparameterization). The theorem statement, and the abstract's 'the scalar certificate is uniquely determined', claim more than the argument supports.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Hereafter, we assume $a_* \ne b_*$ and prove the uniqueness of the positive

The remaining case
$a_*=b_*$ corresponds to the balanced terminal manifold $K_{\overline \delta}$, and will therefore be
contained in the terminal manifold associated with the resulting family.

Thus the unbalanced minimizers sweep out the full

issues.failure_explanation: The Lagrange-multiplier computation shows only that any level set $\{x^\top P x=1\}$ that contains an unbalanced global minimizer $x_*$ must equal the ellipse $E(\delta(a_*))$. Nothing in the argument shows (i) that every level set with parameter in $[\delta_{\mathrm{th}},\overline\delta)$ contains such a minimizer, (ii) that unbalanced minimizers cannot lie in the terminal set $K_{\overline\delta}$ (asserted without proof), or (iii) that the abstract family has no additional level sets between the ellipses $E(\delta)$. The concluding sentence infers uniqueness of all nonterminal level sets from the fact that $\delta(a_*)=4a_*^2/(a_*^4+1)$ ranges over $(0,2)$, which is a property of the answer, not of an arbitrary admissible family. Closing the gap requires a separate argument using the nesting axiom (e.g., that $K_{\overline\delta}$ is an axis segment containing no unbalanced minimizer, that the set of realized ellipses is an upper interval, and that any sandwiched level set coincides with an ellipse by continuity of the nested family).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a lemma: using A2–A4, show that $K_{\overline\delta}$ (an intersection of nested symmetric ellipses of measure zero) contains no unbalanced minimizer, so every unbalanced minimizer lies on some level set, which must be an ellipse $E(\delta)$; then use strict nesting and continuity of $E(\cdot)$ to show every level set with parameter $\ge\delta_{\mathrm{th}}$ is sandwiched and hence equals some $E(\delta)$.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the uniqueness theorem (even in its corrected 'up to reparameterization' form) is incomplete; the same gap affects the appeals to this theorem in Appendix G (signal-block determination) and Remark rmk:ext_to_quartic, which rely on level sets containing unbalanced stationary points.
issues.title: Uniqueness proof only determines level sets that contain an unbalanced minimizer; extension to all nonterminal level sets is unjustified
issues.why_classification: The conclusion is recoverable, but only via a new, nontrivial topological argument not present in the source; no advertised result is lost.
